sources.excerpt: Guitar Pedal X - GPX Blog - Rose Morris teams up with ThorpyFX to bring back its much celebrated Shaftesbury Duo Fuzz / Super-Fuzz ao link News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index Enter a search term Search Remember Login Register | Reset Password Xploration • Curation • Recommendation News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index Enter a search term Search Remember Login Register | Reset Password Filter content by area of interest Amps Boost and Overdrive Delay Distortion Fuzz Guitars Modulation Pitch Reverb Utility All All Rose Morris teams up with ThorpyFX to bring back its much celebrated Shaftesbury Duo Fuzz / Super-Fuzz Feb 14, 2025 08:00 by  Stefan Karlsson Fuzz Rose Morris Shaftersbury Silicon Fuzz Super-Fuzz Style + - Full Article Read Summary Key Points Rose Morris and ThorpyFX revived the Shaftesbury Duo Fuzz in Compact (£249) and Heritage (£349) editions. As of the release announcement, the prices were £249 and £349. Compact uses aluminium and Schottky diodes; Heritage uses folded steel, NOS Germanium Diodes, and original circuitboard sizing. Both follow the authentic, lower-output silicon Super-Fuzz sound. Compact adds footswitchable Flat/Scooped Tone; Heritage has a side-mounted switch. Pete Townshend, Steve Hackett, Miles Kane and Dave Stewart used the original. It is the author’s 24th Super-Fuzz, with no official demos yet. Note that there are 2 pedals in this release - a more practical sort of standard Compact one, and a more accurate full replica one too. There are a few differences besides the obvious size and enclosure variations. The Heritage Edition (£349) is a fully period-correct vintage reproduction - with the same circuitboard and sizing of the the original. The Heritage edition also has NOS Germanium Diodes, while the Compact Edition (£249) makes use of a pair of near identical Schottky Didoes. I am ever the more practical musician - so I’m always going to go for the more flexible and user-friendly experience. And I really like having the 2 Tone Options (Flat / Scooped) on the left-hand footswitch versus a side-mounted switch on the Heritage version. Controls - Balance (Level), Expander (Fuzz Intensity), Tone Footswitch : Flat / Scooped, On/Off Footswitch. The Univox / Shin-Ei / Honey Super-Fuzz was OEM manufactured for several different brands from 1968 onwards - including Rose Morris’s Shaftesbury imprint - and all of these following ones! : Ace Tone, Alex, Apollo, Aria, Avora, Boomer, Bruno, Companion, Crestwood, Crown, Diamond, Electra, Elk, Excetro, Goya, Greco, Hohner, Jax, Kimbara, Kent, LRE, Lord, Luxor, Mana, Marlboro, Maya, Mayfair, Melos, Memphis, Mica, National, Nomad, Northland, Oscar, Pax, Rands, Royal, Sekova, Selmner, Teisco, Telestar, Tempo, Thomas, Uecks, and Zenta. Thorpy was commissioned to make fully authentic vintage style versions - working from replicating an original Shaftesbury DuoFuzz which is part of Rose Morris’s permanent collection. So these Compact and Heritage versions very much have vintage specs, and slightly lower output profiles / volume - exactly in line with the originals. S
